6.1 — Gravity & Jump: AddForce Impulse

You are in the cave now (5.3), and caves have holes, ledges, and reasons to leave the ground. Today you give your character a jump — one line of physics — and then spend the rest of the hour tuning what that line feels like.

Predict First ~10 min

Read the jump branch inside PlayerController.Update — the part that only exists because isPlatformer is true:

[SerializeField] private float jumpForce = 10f;
private Rigidbody2D rb;

...

if (isPlatformer)
{
    if (Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.Space))
    {
        rb.AddForce(Vector2.up * jumpForce, ForceMode2D.Impulse);
    }
}

Predict before running: AddForce with mode Impulse applies an INSTANT kick, not a steady push — like a flick, not a hand. So why does the player keep RISING after the flick ends? What field from 5.3 pulls them back down, and what number controls how floaty the arc is?

Second prediction: you hold Space down for two whole seconds. One jump or several? Why does GetKeyDown (not GetKey) decide this — and what would rocket boots feel like with GetKey?

Socratic

Every jump you have ever felt was three numbers arguing: jumpForce up, gravityScale down, mass resisting. Which two of those live on the player in the Inspector right now — and which one would you tune FIRST to make the jump feel heavy rather than floaty?

Build Lab ~25 min

Step 1 — the flick. In the Platformer scene, press Play and tap Space. If the jump already works, do NOT move on: you are going to rebuild it anyway. Comment out the AddForce line, tap Space (nothing — you are a top-down ghost in a platformer body), and retype it. That gap — "nothing" then "flight" — is the whole lesson. AddForce says: apply this force NOW, physics takes over. Impulse means the "now" is one frame, not a dribble.

Step 2 — the tuning triangle. Three knobs, one jump. Change ONE at a time and write one sentence of feel:

KnobTryFeel sentence
jumpForce10 → 15 → 5"how high" — arcade vs. ant
rb.gravityScale2 → 4 → 1"how heavy" — moon vs. balloon
rb.mass1 → 5 → 0.5how much the SAME force moves you
Note the trap: raising mass makes you fall faster AND jump lower. The starter keeps mass at 1 and tunes the other two — that is the convention most platformers use: keep one knob boring so the other two mean something.

Step 3 — read the arc. Jump next to a wall and trace the shape your character draws. It is a parabola: the flick gives upward velocity, gravity subtracts from it every frame (that is literally what gravityScale does — a multiplier on the engine's 9.81 m/s²). Halfway up, velocity passes through zero — that hang time at the apex is the floatiest moment in the game, and 6.3 will weaponize it.

Bug Hunt: The broken jump

  1. Delete the ForceMode2D.Impulse argument (keep the force). Tap Space. Describe the difference — and explain it using "one frame vs. dribble."
  2. Swap Vector2.up for Vector2.down. What did you build instead of a jump — and what kind of game mechanic IS that (a stomp!)?
  3. Set gravityScale to 0 in the Platformer scene (the branch in Start sets it for you — fight it). What happens after ONE jump, and why does "no gravity" and "no jump" end in the same place?
  4. Change GetKeyDown to GetKey and hold Space. Count the jumps per second — and why will 6.2 make this bug impossible rather than merely annoying?
Tinker ~10 min

Tinker: Jump design

  1. Tune a "sticky" jump: gravityScale 4, jumpForce 14. Then a "floaty" one: 1.5 and 8. Which fits a cave full of spikes — and why do most action games choose sticky?
  2. Variable jump height (the classic): release Space early to jump LOW. What would you cut off mid-flight — hint: the rb's velocity.y? Why is that fairer than it sounds?
  3. Hard: jump on a MOVING platform. What does AddForce do to the platform's velocity — and why do real games parent the rider instead?

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Explain Impulse vs. continuous force in feel-words
  • Tune jumpForce / gravityScale / mass and say what each changes
  • Explain the parabola: flick up, gravity subtracts, apex, fall
  • Explain GetKeyDown vs GetKey for one-shot actions
